prompts.option-1.png:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: preview-only Vedansh native mobile Katha reading screen.
Design direction: Illustrated folio.
Create a realistic, production-quality UI design with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Target dimensions: 390 x 844 logical pixels, portrait mobile app content only. No device bezel, phone body, notch, Dynamic Island, OS status bar, clock, signal, battery, home indicator, browser chrome, device mask, or device shadow.
Inputs: Image 1 is the ORIGINAL plain English Katha screen, for exact reading content and existing controls. Image 2 is the current illustrated Katha reader, for existing design language and layout reference. Image 3 is the existing Vishnu/Narayana thematic artwork, for the devotional subject and composition.
Goal: make existing reading cards, visuals and background visually delightful while keeping long prose comfortably readable and the implementation lightweight. This is a visual proposal, not a production screenshot. Preserve all existing reader functions; do not invent extra features, badges, tabs, controls or story content.
Keep the warm manuscript house design: page #F3E7C9, opaque reading paper #F8EFD6, dark ink #1A0E03, muted ink #6E5230, saffron #B8621B, saffron-deep #8A3E0B and restrained gold #A67C34. Cormorant Garamond for English title/body and Inter for small chrome. Reading text 20px with 33px line height, clear hierarchy, comfortable reading length. Hindi switch uses a serif Devanagari face. 22px page gutters, 18px card radius. Body text should be dark and never have detailed artwork behind it.
Layout strategy: keep a single illustrated reading folio. Place the existing back arrow, centered reader title and 1/5 counter at the top, the thin saffron progress rule, then the existing compact share, हिन्दी/English switch and Listen controls. Inside one opaque paper reading card, use a beautiful 140px opening painting, then PART · 1/5, the chapter heading, a fine house divider and the scrollable prose. No cards within cards; the artwork is a natural illustration on the paper, without its own box. Keep the section dots in a slim bottom rail outside the scrolling prose.
Improve the reference artwork into a softly illuminated watercolor miniature with selective saffron, antique gold, warm rose and muted peacock pigment confined to the illustration. Preserve the exact depicted subjects, poses, attributes and relationships from Image 3; keep Vishnu, Lakshmi, Shesha and the lotus figure complete and uncropped. No new people, invented event or rearranged iconography. Fade only the surrounding painted paper into the reading card. Use restrained lotus-edge linework at very low opacity on the outer page, and clean margins; no faux cracked paper, heavy vignette or repetitive busy texture.
Visible text (verbatim): "Shri Satyanarayana Vrat Katha", "1 / 5", "हिन्दी", "English", "Listen", "PART · 1/5", "Chapter 1: The sages ask and the vow is revealed".
Unabridged scrollable body begins verbatim: "In the sacred forest of Naimisharanya, eighty-eight thousand sages once gathered, and folding their hands they approached Suta ji, the knower of the Puranas, saying, 'O great sage, in this age of Kali, when the strength of the Vedas and of penance grows feeble, by what simple means may a person fulfil their heart's desires and attain liberation? Pray tell us a vow that yields great fruit from little effort.'"
Show the start of that real prose naturally continuing below the viewport, without cramped type, clipped letters or invented copy. Use realistic breathing space and one focused reading experience.
Performance constraints: static small artwork suitable for content-hashed WebP on R2, reuse one painting for theme and opening, no animation, blur, parallax, video, new font families or visually heavy effects. Layout must reserve the illustration space so remote loading never moves text. Offline can substitute the existing neutral manuscript in the same slot. Controls and text remain usable instantly.
Current date anchor 2026-10-09; no dates need be shown. Do not put the direction name, option numbers or explanatory annotations in the image.
